title: RR Article 5 Region 1 allocations for the bands of Table 21-4 (Finland)

source.document: ITU Radio Regulations, Edition of 2024, Volume 1, Article 5

scope: Region 1 column only, for every Table 21-4 band applicable in Finland. Additional allocations made in footnotes for all of Region 1 (5.447B, 5.487A, 5.538, 5.540) are included with their basis. Footnotes that name countries were checked for Finland; only 5.536B/5.536C (25.5-27 GHz earth stations) name Finland and they do not change allocations.
service_tokens: Space services use the tokens of station_classes.json (FSS, BSS, MSS, RDSS, METSAT, EESS, EESS_ACTIVE, SR, SO, ISS). Terrestrial: FIXED, MOBILE, METAIDS, BROADCASTING, RADIOLOCATION, RADIONAV, AERONAV, AMATEUR. Passive or non-transmitting: EESS_PASSIVE, SR_PASSIVE, RA. SFTS = standard frequency and time signal-satellite.

transcription.method: Read from rendered PDF pages and cross-checked against pdftotext layout text.

notes.MOBILE: Includes 'MOBILE except aeronautical mobile' and 'LAND MOBILE'; any terrestrial mobile allocation counts as the mobile service for No. 21.16.
notes.5.447B: Additional primary FSS (space-to-Earth) allocation in 5 150-5 216 MHz, limited to feeder links of non-GSO MSS systems.
notes.5.487A: Additional primary FSS (space-to-Earth) allocation in Region 1 11.7-12.5 GHz, limited to non-geostationary systems.
notes.5.458B: FSS space-to-Earth in 6 700-7 075 MHz is limited to feeder links for non-GSO MSS systems.
notes.5.538: Additional primary FSS (space-to-Earth) allocation in 27.500-27.501 and 29.999-30.000 GHz for up-link power-control beacons.
notes.5.540: Additional secondary FSS (space-to-Earth) allocation in 27.501-29.999 GHz for up-link power-control beacons.
notes.5.554A: FSS space-to-Earth in 47.5-47.9, 48.2-48.54 and 49.44-50.2 GHz is limited to geostationary satellites.
notes.5.499A: FSS space-to-Earth in 13.4-13.65 GHz is limited to geostationary-satellite systems.
notes.5.477: Fixed is primary in 9 800-10 000 MHz only in the listed countries; Finland is not listed, so it is secondary in Finland.
notes.5.544: In 31-31.3 GHz the Table 21-4 limits apply to the space research service (explicit, despite the secondary allocation).
